metadata.board_title:
BOARD OF SECONDARY EDUCATION, A.P. :: VIJAYAWADA
SSC PUBLIC EXAMINATIONS - MODEL ASSESSMENT
metadata.subject: GENERAL SCIENCE - PAPER I (PHYSICAL SCIENCE : PHYSICS)
instructions: First 15 minutes are allotted for reading the question paper thoroughly.
All answers must be written in the answer booklet provided.
The paper consists of 4 Sections: Section I, II, III and IV.
Internal choice is available in Section IV (8 Marks questions).
Draw neat, labeled circuit diagrams and ray diagrams wherever required.

sections.title: SECTION - I
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions. Each question carries 1 Mark.

questions.question: State Ohm's law and write its fundamental mathematical relationship at constant temperature.
Why is tungsten metal exclusively used for the filament of incandescent electric lamps?
A convex lens has a focal length of $f = +20\text{ cm}$. What is the optical power ($P$) of this lens?
Which of the following physical rules is applied to determine the direction of induced electric current in an AC generator?
Name the eye defect in which a person can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly. Which corrective lens is prescribed?
Why does the clear sky appear blue during the daytime? State Rayleigh's law of scattering ($I \propto \frac{1}{\lambda^4}$).

sections.title: SECTION - II
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions in 3 to 4 sentences/steps. Each question carries 2 Marks.

questions.question: An object $5\text{ cm}$ in height is placed at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ in front of a convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$. Use the lens formula $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u}$ to find the position ($v$) and nature of the image.
Differentiate between Ohmic Conductors and Non-Ohmic Conductors with two suitable examples for each.
Why are electrical appliances in domestic household circuits connected in parallel rather than in series? Give two important practical reasons.
What is a Solenoid? How does the magnetic field inside a current-carrying long cylindrical solenoid behave?

sections.title: SECTION - III
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions in 5 to 6 sentences/steps. Each question carries 4 Marks.

questions.question:
Draw neat ray diagrams showing the formation of image by a convex lens when an object is placed:
i) At the center of curvature ($2F_1$)
ii) Between the optical center ($O$) and the principal focus ($F_1$).
In each case, specify the position, relative size, and real/virtual nature of the image.

questions.heading: The following experimental observations of potential difference ($V$) and current ($I$) were recorded to verify Ohm's Law:
sub_questions: i) What conclusion do you infer regarding the relationship between $V$ and $I$?
ii) What physical property is represented by the constant ratio $\frac{V}{I}$?
iii) Calculate the electrical resistance of the given conductor wire.
iv) What will be the geometric nature and slope of the $V\text{-}I$ graph plotted from this data?

questions.question:
Explain the vision defect Myopia (Near-sightedness):
i) State two physiological causes of Myopia.
ii) Draw two neat ray diagrams: one showing a myopic eye, and the second showing its optical correction using a concave lens.

An electric iron of resistance $20\ \Omega$ takes a current of $5\text{ A}$. Calculate the heat energy ($H = I^2 R t$) developed in $30\text{ seconds}$. If two such heaters and four $50\text{ W}$ bulbs run for $4\text{ hours}$ daily, calculate the total electrical energy consumed in kWh (commercial units) in a $30$-day month.

sections.title: SECTION - IV
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions. Each question carries 8 Marks. There is an INTERNAL CHOICE (A or B) for each question.

choice_a.title: A) Laboratory Experiment to Verify Ohm's Law
choice_a.format:
Describe an experiment to verify that the current flowing through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends ($V \propto I$) at constant temperature.

Structure your answer under the following headings:
• Aim of the experiment
• Apparatus Required (Battery, Key, Ammeter, Voltmeter, Rheostat, Nichrome wire)
• Circuit Diagram description (Series and Parallel connections)
• Step-by-step Experimental Procedure
• Tabular form for recording $V$ and $I$ observations
• Graph plotting & Precautions to avoid heating the conductor

choice_b.title: B) Faraday's Electromagnetic Induction Experiment
choice_b.format:
Describe an experiment to demonstrate the phenomenon of Electromagnetic Induction using a wire coil and a bar magnet.

Structure your answer under the following headings:
• Aim of the activity
• Apparatus Required (Insulated copper wire coil, Sensitive Galvanometer, Strong Bar Magnet)
• Step-by-step Procedure
• Observations: (i) When North pole is pushed into coil, (ii) When magnet is held stationary, (iii) When magnet is pulled out
• Conclusion and statement of Faraday's Law of Induction ($e = -N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t}$)

choice_a.title: A) Electric Motor (DC Motor): Principle, Construction & Working
choice_a.format:
Explain the working of an Electric Motor (DC Motor) which converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.

Structure your answer as follows:
• Working Principle (Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field)
• Construction: Explain functions of (i) Rectangular Armature Coil, (ii) Strong Permanent Horseshoe Magnet, (iii) Split-Ring Commutator, (iv) Carbon Brushes
• Step-by-step Working Mechanism over a half-rotation and role of commutator in reversing current
• State Fleming's Left-Hand Rule used to determine the force on arms of the coil

choice_b.title: B) Refraction and Dispersion of Light through a Triangular Glass Prism
choice_b.format:
Explain the behavior of light when passing through a triangular glass prism.

Structure your answer as follows:
• State Snell's Law of Refraction ($n = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r}$)
• Describe an activity to trace the path of a ray of light through a glass prism, labeling Angle of Incidence ($i$), Angle of Refraction ($r$), Angle of Emergence ($e$), and Angle of Deviation ($D$)
• Explain the phenomenon of Dispersion of White Light into seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR)
• Explain why violet light deviates the most while red light deviates the least in terms of wavelength ($\lambda$) and refractive index ($n$)
